records.name: Berean Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A Presbyterian church near Broad and Diamond streets on the Temple University campus that worships on Sunday and streams services online.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship in person or watch the live stream. The ministries and special events pages list no details yet, so ask the church office about other activities.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am, streamed on Facebook Live, with a 12:15 pm conference call service

first_step.how: Come to the 11 am Sunday service in person, or watch the live stream. The contact form is the way to ask questions.
first_step.basis: The homepage says visitors will be welcomed and invites people to come in person on Sunday, with a contact form for questions. No newcomer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship is at 11 am at the church building on North Broad Street, and it is also streamed live on Facebook. The site does not say how long a service runs, whether there is a children's program, or what it costs, so the contact form is the best place to ask.
first_visit_tips: The church is at 2101 North Broad Street, at the corner of Broad and Diamond streets.
The site does not describe parking or transit, so check your route before you go.
The 11 am stream is on Facebook Live. The site says you may need to send the pastor a Facebook friend request to see it.

records.notes: Deep pass. The ministries page holds only brochure images, which could not be read, and the special events page lists no dated items. The site footer reads 2018, which is not counted as evidence, so status stays probably_active with low confidence. Phone and email come from the regional presbytery listing (tier 1), since the church contact page shows only a form. Cost, parking, transit and children's programs are not stated on the site.

records.name: Bethesda Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A Presbyterian church in Northeast Philadelphia with adult Sunday school and an 11 am worship service, also shared online.
records.what_you_do: Join adult Sunday school at 9:30 am or worship at 11 am, in person or online. The office can answer questions about ministries.

schedule.text: Adult Sunday school at 9:30 am and worship at 11 am on Sundays. The worship service is also livestreamed.

first_step.how: Come to 11 am worship on a Sunday, or email or call the church office to ask about joining a group.
first_step.basis: The site says visitors are welcome to join its activities and events, invites people to visit in person, and gives a contact route for questions.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday starts with adult Sunday school at 9:30 am, and worship is at 11 am. The site describes the church as a safe place to ask questions. It does not list costs, a children's program, or how long services last.
first_visit_tips: The office is open Tuesday to Friday, 9 am to 3:30 pm, so call or email then if you have questions before you visit.
The site lists no parking or transit details, so check the route to 808 Red Lion Road before you go.
Worship is livestreamed from 11 am on Sundays, if you want to try it from home first.

records.notes: Deep pass. The calendar page lists no dated events, and the footer reads 2025, which is not counted as evidence. A banner says the church is back on livestream and Zoom, but it has no date. The ministries page names no specific ministries. The site has no parking, transit, accessibility or children's program details. Status stays probably_active.

records.name: Black Writers Museum
records.summary: A museum in the Historic Vernon House in Vernon Park that shows classic and modern Black writers and their books. It holds a free family festival in Germantown and has volunteer and donation pages.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the site's volunteer page, come to the free festival, or call to arrange a visit by appointment.

schedule.text: Museum visits are by appointment, and the museum is closed on major holidays. The free family festival in Vernon Park is a summer event.

cost.text: The festival is free. The site does not list a fee for visits.

first_step.how: Call 267-297-3078 to arrange a visit or ask about volunteering, or fill in the volunteer form on the museum's site.
first_step.basis: The festival is free and open to all ages. Visits need an appointment, and the volunteer form is a clear way in. The site does not describe a first visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: Visits are by appointment, so you call or use the contact form first. The site does not say how long a visit takes or whether tours are offered. Volunteers fill in a form with their name, phone, email, and address, and the free summer festival is a family event with music, spoken word, and vendors.
first_visit_tips: Call 267-297-3078 before you come, since visits need an appointment.
The site does not mention parking, transit, or wheelchair access, so ask when you call.
The museum is in the Historic Vernon House inside Vernon Park.

records.notes: Status set to dormant because the newest dated item readable on the museum's site is the festival page, which describes the 2018 and 2019 festivals. Copyright footers (2026) are not counted. A search result listed a 2026 festival at the museum, but the Historic Germantown event page for it returned a 404 and the museum listing on that calendar shows no events, so the 2026 festival is not recorded. Owner may want to confirm by phone before publishing. Weekly hours in a search snippet conflict with the museum's own by-appointment wording, so no weekly hours are recorded. A SEPTA bus and regional rail stop named in a search snippet is not on the museum's pages, so it is left out of access notes. The Urban Affairs Coalition is named only as the museum's fiscal sponsor, so it is not listed as a lead.

records.name: Blessings Across Borders
records.notes: Hidden for owner review, not a final decision. The closest hidden reason is out_of_scope, since no exact reason fits. (1) The about page lists a program line about marriages for underprivileged children with no explanation, which could point to child marriage and needs checking before anything is published. (2) The home page says it is a preview site, one page reads as served from a preview address, and the impact counters all show zero. (3) There is no volunteer role or sign-up route, only donations (the Donate Now link goes to an external crowdfunding page) and an email. Tier 1 IRS and nonprofit listings matched the name and EIN. The owner should confirm the real domain and the program wording before any change to publish.

records.name: Block by Block Philly
records.summary: A volunteer-run nonprofit that organizes cleanups against litter and illegal dumping across Philadelphia. It also hosts block parties and works with schools and businesses on clean streets.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a listed cleanup on the Get Involved page, start a group cleanup of your own, or clean your own block and submit your bags through the trash form.

schedule.text: Cleanups are posted on the Get Involved page as they are scheduled, so check there for the next date.

locations.label: Meeting point for a listed cleanup (varies by event)

cost.text: Free to join. Donations and sponsorships are optional.

first_step.how: Pick a listed cleanup on the Get Involved page, RSVP through the link on its event page, and meet at the posted spot.
first_step.basis: The site says events are family-friendly and welcoming to all, and it explains how to join a listed cleanup, with an RSVP link on each event page.
first_step.what_to_expect: A cleanup is a group outing at a posted spot and time. Organizers provide vests, gloves, tools, and water, and the group gives guidance on the work. The site does not say how long each cleanup lasts, so check the event page.
first_visit_tips: The site says you only need to bring your energy and commitment, since the group supplies vests, gloves, tools, and water.
The train tracks cleanup recommends ages 18 and up, so check each event page for age guidance.
The site gives no parking or transit details, so check the event page or ask the group before you go.

records.notes: last_sign_of_life 2026-10 rests on the Clean-Off 2026 page, which states its October 1 to 31, 2026 dates. Cleanup dates shown without a year (October 10, 12 and 14, and a November 7 community day) are not used. The tier 1 October 10 train tracks cleanup is a one-time event, so its day and time were moved out of schedule, and its age advice is kept in the tips. Homies Helping Homies is named as a cleanup partner on the homepage; no website of its own was linked from the pages read, so it is listed only as a lead. The Know What to Throw workshop is run by the group, in person or virtually, and is not a separate record.

records.name: Blockchain at Penn
records.summary: A student group for undergraduate, graduate and MBA students who want to learn about blockchain, crypto and Web3. It works with partners on education and research, and sends committee members to conferences and hackathons.
records.what_you_do: Come to the education seminar, which is open to anyone with no prior knowledge needed, and join the listserv for recruiting news. Committee members get access to club-wide events and trips.

schedule.text: The education seminar runs each fall and spring semester.

first_step.how: Attend the education seminar in the fall or spring, no prior knowledge needed, and join the club's listserv for recruiting news through the link on its Penn Clubs page.
first_step.basis: The Penn Clubs listing says the education seminar is available to all and needs no prior knowledge, and the club gives a listserv route for recruiting news.
first_step.what_to_expect: The education seminar needs no prior knowledge and is aimed at people new to crypto and blockchain. The site does not say how long a session lasts, where it meets, or what it costs. Committee members get access to club-wide events and trips to conferences and hackathons.
first_visit_tips: Ask the club by email about the current seminar date and place before you come, since the club's events list was empty when checked.
This is a Penn student group, so ask first whether non-students can take part. The seminar itself is listed as open to all.

records.notes: The club's home page lists its 2026 conference on March 27 and 28, 2026, which is the basis for last_sign_of_life 2026-03. The about page says the conference runs each February, which conflicts, so no conference month is recorded. The Penn Clubs listing names a club officer with a personal email; it is left out, and only the group email is published. The seminar's cost and meeting place are not stated on any page read.

records.name: B'nai Abraham Chabad
records.summary: A Chabad congregation at 527 Lombard Street that invites Jews of all backgrounds to study, pray, and make friends. It offers adult Torah study and links to a preschool and a Hebrew school.
records.what_you_do: Join a Torah studies season or the Sunday morning Talmud class, or come to a morning, Shabbat, or High Holiday service. Membership details are on a separate page.

schedule.text: Weekday morning prayers at 7:15 am, Saturday services at 9:30 am, and Sunday and holiday services at 8:30 am. A Talmud class meets Sunday mornings from 9:30 to 10:30 am. Friday night services begin 10 minutes before sundown, or at 7 pm in summer. Weekday evening services need a phone call to confirm.

cost.text: Membership dues: individual $480 a year, family $720 a year, student $180 a year. The site does not say whether non-members pay for services or classes.

first_step.how: Register for a Torah studies session through the site's Register Here form, or call the office at 215-238-2100 to ask about attending services.
first_step.basis: The Torah studies page says classes are open to everyone of all abilities and gives a register form, and the membership page invites new people to join. The site does not describe a first visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: Services are designed to make everyone feel welcome, and the prayers use Hebrew and English prayer books. The Sunday morning Talmud class runs from 9:30 to 10:30 am and uses an English translation. The site does not say whether non-members can attend services, how a first visit works, or what a service involves.
first_visit_tips: Call (215) 238-2100 before you come, since the site does not describe a first visit.
Evening minyan times are not fixed, so call to confirm before coming in the evening.
The site lists no parking or transit details, so ask when you call.

records.notes: The Hebrew school and preschool are separate external sites linked from the homepage, so they are not described as run from this site. Torah studies seasons are labeled 5786 (the Hebrew year) with no Gregorian dates on the pages read, so status stays probably_active. Membership dues are recorded as yearly rates only. The directions page names no SEPTA line or stop, so no nearest stop is recorded. Whether non-members can attend services is not stated.

leads_only.name: Homies Helping Homies
leads_only.note: Named as a partner on a South Philly cleanup listing on the Block by Block site. No website of its own was linked from the pages read, so it was not fetched.

notes: Seven groups in the batch, each given a deep pass. Verdict counts: publish 6, hide 1. One WebSearch used of the one allowed (Black Writers Museum festival). 33 fetches in total: 31 on the groups' own sites or group-run pages (Berean 4, Bethesda 6, Black Writers Museum 5, Blessings 4, Block by Block 4, Blockchain 3, Chabad 5), plus 2 on Historic Germantown pages, one of which returned 404. No blocked pages, bot checks or 403 responses; no rate limiting seen. Key findings: Black Writers Museum set to dormant, since the newest readable dated item is from 2019. Block by Block and Blockchain at Penn are active on written 2026 dates. Blessings Across Borders is hidden for owner review, because of an unexplained program line about marriages for underprivileged children, a preview-domain site, and no volunteer route; the owner should decide before it is published. Berean, Bethesda and Chabad stay probably_active. Personal contact details (a club officer's email) are left out, per the ethics rules. Budget: WebSearch cap reached, fetch budget not exhausted.
